correctness.rationale: For n=(a,c)_b the divisibility condition is exactly a+c | a(b-1). Separating c=0 and uniquely writing a=g*u, a+c=g*v with gcd(u,v)=1 gives v|(b-1) and an exact g-range from the two digit bounds, proving the formula bijectively. Two universal disjoint families give 2b-3. For odd prime b-1, divisor support forces every positive final digit into the digit-sum-(b-1) family; for composite b-1 an explicit proper-divisor witness lies outside both families. The b=2 and b=3 boundary cases are stated separately. A fresh direct checker agrees through base 300.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete and nontrivial divisor-lattice parameterization of the first nontrivial digit stratum, not merely a bounded census. Its sharp lower bound has an arithmetic equality condition: for every b>=4, the minimum population occurs exactly when b-1 is prime. This provides a natural exact finite counterpart to fixed-base asymptotic Niven theory and a structural explanation of how divisors of the base-minus-one create additional solutions.
